newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan elections stalls telephone sale.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan elections stalls telephone sale.

text.p: The partial sale of Nicaragua's state-run telephone company was postponed on Thursday because of buyer fears over the results of its Oct. 20 elections, the finance minister said.

The opening of the bids for the 40 percent of Empresa Nicaraguense de Telecomunicaciones S.A. (Enitel) shares being sold was postponed at the last minute to March 31, 1997, Finance Minister Emilio Pereira, head of the Enitel privatisation committee, said at a press conference.
"The interested companies asked us to postpone the auction until after the elections, including until after the change of government on Jan. 10," Pereira said.

Pereira said members of the privatisation committee, made up of representatives from the government, Enitel and labour, thought investors would offer far less money for the Enitel shares due to uncertainty over the election results.
"Due to the political uncertainty, the bids offered could have been 20-30 percent of the normal value of the company," he said.
Nicaragua's vote pits Arnoldo Aleman of the right-wing Liberal Alliance against former President Daniel Ortega of the left-wing Sandinista Front in a neck-in-neck battle for the presidency.
The possibility of a victory by the Sandinistas, who governed Nicaragua from 1979-1990 with the backing of the Soviet Union and Cuba, has raised fears among sectors of the business community.
